name: Rofanseilbahn
kurzbeschreibung: The Rofanseilbahn cable car in Maurach at Lake Achensee reaches 1,840 m in the Rofan Mountains, featuring the AIRROFAN skyglider, the Adlerhorst viewing nest, and panoramic paths.
preis: Hiking trail network freely accessible; cable car ascent/descent and AIRROFAN flight apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Summer operations run daily from early May to early November
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Rofanseilbahn cable car, located in the lakeside village of Maurach at Lake Achensee, unlocks one of the most dramatic mountain scenery and trekking zones in the Northern Limestone Alps. In just a few minutes, the modern aerial tramway ascends nearly 860 vertical metres from its valley station at 980 metres to the top terminal at 1,840 metres above sea level. Stepping off the gondola, visitors are greeted by a breathtaking alpine plateau encircled by the bold limestone horns of the Rofan Range, including the Rofanspitze, Sagzahn, and Gschöllkopf peaks. Far below, the turquoise expanse of Lake Achensee – celebrated as 'Tirol's Fjord' – glistens in all its splendor. Alongside a dense web of panoramic alpine trails and via ferratas, the Rofan is famous for high-adrenaline adventure: aboard the 'AIRROFAN' skyglider, styled like an eagle, thrill-seekers swoop down from Mount Gschöllkopf at speeds reaching 80 km/h. Nearby, the 'Adlerhorst' viewing platform perched at 2,039 metres provides panoramic vistas across the Inn Valley, the Karwendel, and the Zillertal Alps.

Route & Anforderungen

Departing from the Erfurter Hütte mountain hut next to the upper cable car station, hikes cater to every ambition. A popular, family-friendly outing climbs along an easy gravel path in about 45 minutes up to the Adlerhorst viewing platform on the Gschöllkopf (approx. 200 metres elevation gain). Experienced mountaineers tackle the rewarding summit trek up to the Rofanspitze peak (2,259 m), navigating alpine meadows and stony ridges in roughly 1.5 to 2 hours of ascent. For sheer adventure, the five-peak Achensee via ferrata offers world-class climbing. Comfortable sneakers suffice for strolling around the top station meadows; however, ascending Gschöllkopf or Rofanspitze strictly demands supportive, lug-soled mountain boots, weather-resistant apparel, and sun protection (unsuitable for pushchairs).

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists travel via motorway A12 (exit Wiesing/Achensee) along federal road B181 into Maurach at Lake Achensee. Ample parking bays are located directly at the valley terminal (parking validated for cable car ticket holders). Rail passengers travel to Jenbach station and connect via the historic Achensee steam cog railway or regular VVT buses straight to the lift station.

Tipps

Settle onto the panoramic sun deck of the historic Erfurter Hütte right beside the mountain terminal. Savoring their famous fluffy Kaiserschmarrn with lingonberry jam while admiring the turquoise waters of Lake Achensee far below is a quintessentially Tyrolean indulgence.
